assessment.summary: BTK (Q06187) is one of the best-validated and most successfully drugged kinase targets in oncology and immunology, with 6 approved small-molecule inhibitors, over 21,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 170 PDB structures including ultra-high-resolution ligand-bound complexes. The target has overwhelming structural, chemical, and clinical evidence supporting high druggability, with ongoing innovation including non-covalent inhibitors and PROTACs addressing resistance mechanisms.
evidence_gaps: Resistance mechanisms (e.g., C481S mutation to covalent inhibitors) limit the utility of first-generation drugs, though non-covalent inhibitors and degraders are being developed to address this
Long-term safety profile of newer agents (pirtobrutinib, PROTACs) in broader patient populations still accumulating
Biomarker-driven patient stratification for optimal inhibitor selection remains incompletely defined
PROTAC and degrader modalities are still in early-to-mid clinical development; their comparative efficacy vs. inhibitors is not yet fully established
